l4_steps.name: Extract completed duty periods from crew system
l4_steps.input: Flight completion signals and crew check-in/check-out events
l4_steps.output: Raw duty period records per crew member for the pay period
l4_steps.kpi: Data extraction completeness ≥99.9% of operated flights
l4_steps.pain_point: Late ACARS sign-off events or manual overrides in Jeppesen can produce duplicate or null duty records, requiring manual reconciliation before payroll can proceed

l4_steps.name: Validate actual block times against ACARS data
l4_steps.input: ACARS OUT/OFF/ON/IN timestamps for each flight leg
l4_steps.output: Validated block-hours per leg with variance flags
l4_steps.kpi: Block-time discrepancy rate <0.5% of legs per pay cycle
l4_steps.pain_point: ACARS message loss over oceanic tracks or VHF dropouts can leave gaps requiring manual entry from paper OFP, introducing audit risk

l4_steps.name: Adjudicate duty time discrepancies with crew
l4_steps.input: Flagged duty records with variance >2 minutes vs ACARS
l4_steps.output: Crew-acknowledged corrected duty record; updated in Jeppesen
l4_steps.pain_point: Pilots and cabin crew may contest block-time adjustments that reduce pay — disputes require union observer involvement under most CBAs, extending resolution time

l4_steps.name: Lock finalised duty records for pay period
l4_steps.input: Resolved and validated duty periods for all crew
l4_steps.output: Locked, immutable duty record set ready for pay rule application
l4_steps.kpi: Records locked ≥48 hours before payroll cut-off
l4_steps.pain_point: Late crew changes from irregular ops (IROPS) in the final days of a pay period can force record reopening, risking payroll deadline breach

l4_steps.name: Load CBA pay rules for crew category
l4_steps.input: Locked duty records; active CBA rate tables by crew category (Captain, First Officer, Flight Attendant)
l4_steps.output: Rule set applied to each crew member's records for the pay period
l4_steps.kpi: CBA rule table accuracy rate 100% (zero miscategorisation)
l4_steps.pain_point: Airlines operating multiple crew agreements (pilots vs cabin crew vs contract ground) must maintain separate rate tables in SAP SuccessFactors; version mismatches after CBA renegotiation cause systematic overpayment or underpayment

l4_steps.name: Calculate block/credit hours and per diem
l4_steps.input: Locked duty records; CBA credit-hour conversion rules; per diem rate by city-pair
l4_steps.output: Gross flight pay and per diem amounts per crew member
l4_steps.kpi: Payroll calculation variance vs manual audit sample ≤0.1%
l4_steps.pain_point: CBAs often specify credit hours that differ from actual block hours (e.g. scheduled vs actual, or minimum leg credit), requiring complex conditional logic that is error-prone when rates change mid-year

l4_steps.name: Evaluate and apply minimum-guarantee provisions
l4_steps.input: Calculated credit hours; CBA minimum monthly guarantee thresholds
l4_steps.output: Adjusted pay figure with minimum guarantee top-up applied where triggered
l4_steps.kpi: Minimum guarantee errors detected in post-payroll audit ≤0.2%
l4_steps.pain_point: IROPS-driven trip removals can drop crew below the monthly minimum guarantee, triggering a top-up that must be calculated separately from regular flight pay — SAP wage-type configuration must handle this without double-counting

l4_steps.name: Apply premiums, overrides, and special pay components
l4_steps.input: Base pay calculation; premium triggers (international, redeye, equipment type, senior position)
l4_steps.output: Fully loaded gross pay record including all CBA-mandated premium components
l4_steps.kpi: Premium application accuracy ≥99.8% validated against CBA schedule
l4_steps.pain_point: Introduction of new aircraft types (e.g. A320neo vs B737 MAX) or new international routes creates CBA premium ambiguity until Letter of Agreement (LOA) is ratified — interim pay must be tracked and retroactively corrected

l4_steps.name: Validate daily flight duty period against FAR Part 117
l4_steps.input: Finalised duty records; FAR Part 117 FDP and rest-period limit tables
l4_steps.output: Compliance status flag per duty period (Pass / Warning / Violation)
l4_steps.kpi: FAR Part 117 violation rate 0 per pay cycle; automated check coverage 100%
l4_steps.pain_point: FAR Part 117 FDP limits vary by time-of-day start and number of flight segments — Jeppesen rules engine requires precise configuration and must be updated whenever ICAO or FAA revises rest requirements

l4_steps.name: Check cumulative hours against 28-day and 365-day limits
l4_steps.input: Rolling 28-day and 365-day block-hour totals per crew member
l4_steps.output: Cumulative hours compliance report; breach flags for affected crew
l4_steps.kpi: Zero crew members exceeding FAR Part 117 cumulative limits (100 hrs/28 days; 1,000 hrs/365 days)
l4_steps.pain_point: Cross-border operations and wet-lease arrangements complicate cumulative tracking when hours are flown under different AOCs — hours from partner carriers may not be visible in Jeppesen without manual import

l4_steps.name: Escalate violations and trigger roster correction
l4_steps.input: Breach flags from Step 3.2; crew roster for remainder of period
l4_steps.output: Corrected roster with non-compliant crew removed from duty; compliance memo issued
l4_steps.pain_point: Grounding crew mid-period to cure a FAR Part 117 breach triggers crew-shortage cascades and CBA compensation obligations (deadhead pay, hotel, reassignment premiums) that add unplanned payroll cost

l4_steps.name: Approve validated hours for payroll submission
l4_steps.output: Approved payroll data package signed off by Crew Pay Manager
l4_steps.kpi: Payroll approval completed ≥36 hours before payroll cut-off
l4_steps.pain_point: Approval bottleneck when a single manager owns sign-off for hundreds of crew — absence or IROPS event during cut-off window can delay entire payroll run

l4_steps.name: Transfer approved pay data to SAP SuccessFactors
l4_steps.input: Approved payroll data package from Jeppesen in SFTP/XML format
l4_steps.output: Pay records loaded into SAP SuccessFactors Employee Central Payroll wage types
l4_steps.kpi: File transfer success rate 100%; record reconciliation count match before payroll run
l4_steps.pain_point: Schema mismatches between Jeppesen export format and SAP wage-type structure require a custom integration layer — changes to either system can silently break the interface until the next payroll run

l4_steps.name: Execute payroll calculation run in SAP
l4_steps.input: Loaded wage types; tax tables; statutory deduction rates; benefit deductions
l4_steps.output: Gross-to-net payroll results; payslip data; GL posting document
l4_steps.kpi: Payroll error log: zero critical errors; warning resolution ≤2 hours
l4_steps.pain_point: Multi-state tax residency for crew who live in a different state from their crew base requires correct SAP tax-area assignment — errors create IRS compliance exposure and retroactive correction cost

l4_steps.name: Generate pay advices and post GL entries
l4_steps.output: Digital pay advices distributed to crew; GL postings to crew cost centres
l4_steps.kpi: Pay advice delivery within 24 hours of payroll run; GL posting error rate 0%
l4_steps.pain_point: Crew cost-centre allocation requires splitting payroll costs across multiple operational cost centres when a crew member flew for different fleets or bases in the same period — misallocation distorts fleet P&L reporting

l4_steps.name: Reconcile payroll cost vs crew operations budget
l4_steps.input: GL payroll postings; crew operations budget from SAP CO; headcount actuals
l4_steps.output: Variance report by crew category and cost centre; commentary on material variances
l4_steps.kpi: Payroll-to-budget variance explained ≥95% within 3 business days of payroll run
l4_steps.pain_point: IROPS months generate significant unbudgeted premium and minimum-guarantee costs that distort variance analysis — Finance needs a dedicated IROPS payroll variance code to separate structural from operational pay drivers

l4_steps.name: Generate crew hours utilisation and fatigue report
l4_steps.input: Finalised hours data from Jeppesen; payroll cost data from SAP S/4HANA
l4_steps.output: Monthly crew hours utilisation dashboard; fatigue risk indicator by base
l4_steps.kpi: Crew utilisation rate ≥85% of contractual hours; fatigue indicator trend published ≤5 days post-period
l4_steps.pain_point: Combining hours data from Jeppesen with cost data from SAP requires a data pipeline that must be maintained across system upgrades — ad hoc Tableau reports built on inconsistent extracts produce conflicting crew productivity figures for leadership

l4_steps.name: Archive payroll and hours records per FAA requirements
l4_steps.input: Finalised pay advices; duty records; compliance reports
l4_steps.output: Archived records retained per FAR 121.683 (24 months minimum) with audit trail
l4_steps.kpi: Record archive completeness 100%; retrieval SLA ≤4 hours for FAA audit request
l4_steps.pain_point: FAR 121.683 mandates 24-month retention for crew duty records; GDPR and state privacy laws (CCPA) impose conflicting obligations on how long certain payroll data can be held — retention policy must be reviewed with legal each year
